newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Independent says well set for further growth.
newsitem.headline: Independent says well set for further growth.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc said on Wednesday that the group continued significant expansion during 1996 and was well set for growth in 1997.
"We are well positioned to achieve further profitable growth during the current year," Independent said in a results statement, adding that the group had now become a truly global media company.
It reported a rise of 47 percent in pre-tax profit to 73.5 million Irish pounds for the year to December 27, 1996.
"These results underscore the rapid development of Independent Newspapers as a global media group and enphasise the growth achieved over the past five years," chairman Tony O'Reilly said.
He said pre-tax profit had increased nine-fold and market capitalisation had grown from 115 million Iirsh pounds to 838 million since 1991.
"The companies under our management now have assets in excess of 1.5 billion Irish pounds and employ over 13,500 people worldwide," O'Reilly said.
Independent said operating profit in Ireland was up 33 percent to 34.5 million Irish pounds and operating margins showed further improvement.
It said the Irish divisions advertising income was buoyant on the back of strong economic growth and circulation revenues were also well ahead of the previous year.
In the UK, it said its publishing operations also showed further growth in profits following a 1995 rationalisation programme.
Profits in the UK rose to 3.4 million Irish pounds from 1.4 million.
